**How it works:** Rust allows block comments inside other block comments, and C++ doesn't. The file uses that difference:

```
/* /* */      <- C++: the comment ends here.   Rust: still inside a comment (one level deep)
#if 0         <- C++: skip everything until #endif.   Rust: still a comment
// */         <- C++: an ordinary line comment.   Rust: the comment ends here
...Rust code...
/* /* */      <- C++: skipped by #if 0.   Rust: a comment starts again
#endif
...C++ code...
// */         <- C++: a line comment.   Rust: the comment ends here
```

Both versions do the addition in base 10⁹ chunks rather than with a fixed-size integer, so they don't overflow for large N. With a 64-bit integer, this sequence overflows after f(91).

**Where `rustc` puts the binary:** it writes the executable to the directory you run it from, not next to the source file. Your command `rustc .../polyglot/main.rs && .../polyglot/main N` only works if you run it from inside `polyglot/`. From anywhere else, add `-o /tmp/obench-cell-lv1qvcsi/bench_opencode_polyglot-rust-c_e6op4oks/polyglot/main` to the `rustc` command.
